instructions: Check each entry against the archive text. Set verdict to agree, disagree or partial (some categories or links are right) and explain any disagreement in note. A negative entry claims the item has no category.

entries.text: Branch trial observations. I tested an owned branch sample at press intensity 0.25: it held, with recorded flexibility 0.2. This establishes only that trial condition, not structural safety. A wetting trial failed because no local water was accessible.
entries.note: Agree: "I tested an owned branch sample at press intensity 0.25: it held, with recorded flexibility 0.2" is a trial report sent to sol (event-19-moss-193); no name, norm, invitation, valuation or absent person.

entries.text: A small hazelnut sample opened with my stone on this rock; I separated a pale kernel from the casing. That establishes opening, not food safety: nutrition, toxins and preparation remain unknown. I have not eaten it.
entries.note: Agree: "A small hazelnut sample opened with my stone on this rock; I separated a pale kernel from the casing" is a preparation trial report heard by wren and ivo; no category applies.

entries.text: My own 0.1 hazelnut trial also opened with stone on stone and yielded separated kernel and casing. That confirms mechanical separation only; food safety, toxins and nutrition remain unknown. I have not tasted it.
entries.note: Agree: "My own 0.1 hazelnut trial also opened with stone on stone and yielded separated kernel and casing" is a trial report heard by kai and wren; no category applies.

entries.text: My own 0.1 hazelnut trial fractured the casing with stone on this rock, then separated kernel and fragments. This confirms mechanical opening only; edibility, toxins and nutrition remain unknown. I have not eaten it.
entries.note: Agree: "My own 0.1 hazelnut trial fractured the casing with stone on this rock" is a trial report heard by kai and ivo; no category applies.

entries.text: Four abrasion strokes on my branch with my stone removed 0.04 kg of wood; the tip measured about 26 mm afterward. It was still unfinished at that point. I have not yet tested it in soil.
entries.note: Agree: "Four abrasion strokes on my branch with my stone removed 0.04 kg of wood" reports progress on shaping a digging tool, valued for use; no category applies.

entries.text: My shaped branch displaced no forest soil at load 0.05: the end was too blunt at that load. It remains sound after that stroke. I will try 0.10 once; this does not yet establish a useful digging tool.
entries.note: Agree: "My shaped branch displaced no forest soil at load 0.05" is a tool trial report and "I will try 0.10 once" a personal plan; no category applies.

entries.text: My shaped branch displaced no meadow soil at loads 0.05 and 0.15: both reported a tip too blunt at those loads. I saw your 0.10 forest stroke move a little soil. Different ground and tools limit comparison; I will test 0.25 once here.
entries.note: Agree: "I saw your 0.10 forest stroke move a little soil" addresses ivo, who was 1.8 away and heard it, so no absent person; the rest is a tool trial report and a personal plan.

entries.text: My seven-stroke shaped branch moved 0.00002 m3 of forest soil at load 0.10, penetrating about 8.7 mm. It remains sound with no cracks. Load 0.05 moved none. This verifies a small digging effect here, not performance in other soils.
entries.note: Agree: "My seven-stroke shaped branch moved 0.00002 m3 of forest soil at load 0.10" is a digging-tool trial report heard by wren; no category applies.

entries.text: My meadow stroke at load 0.25 displaced 0.000006 m3, penetrating about 5.8 mm. The branch is sound with no cracks after three use strokes. Loads 0.05 and 0.15 moved none here; this establishes only a small local digging effect.
entries.note: Agree: "My meadow stroke at load 0.25 displaced 0.000006 m3" is a digging-tool trial report heard by lin, kai and ivo; no category applies.
